newsitem.title: UK: Economy growth makes Polish market attractive - HSBC.
newsitem.headline: Economy growth makes Polish market attractive - HSBC.

text.p: The Polish share market is seen remaining attractive in 1997 on the back of buoyant economic growth, a new report by HSBC James Capel said.

"Although cuts in short-term interest rates have come to a temporary halt, the prospects for the Polish equity market in 1997 remain good," HSBC said in the report, published in the November issue of HSBC Emerging Europe Investment Strategy.
The WIG index is currently trading around 13,596 points, down 0.55 percent on the day, and has come off a 1996 high of 15,078.7.
"Buoyant economic growth and an expanding market, with several major new issues over the coming 12 months, will push prices higher," strategist Nigel Rendell said.
HSBC predicted Poland's GDP to rise by five percent in 1997, after its forecast of 5.2 percent this year.
"Based on the continuing strength of the domestic economy our favoured sectors include food, brewing and construction," HSBC said.
Corporate earnings will reflect the economic strengthening by an earnings per share growth of 20 percent in 1997, up from an estimated 15 percent in 1996, it said.
Interest rates trends give less support to the market.

"Prospects of a cut in short-term interest rates faded following comments from the NBP that real interest rates are to low," the research said. "It now looks like rates will stay at current levels for at least the next three to six months."
